denylist: Any third-party SaaS provider (unless explicitly reconfirmed as owned)
Any shared CDN edge (Cloudflare/Fastly/etc. infrastructure itself)
Any asset that resolves to a shared hosting provider IP not exclusively owned by AuSecurity

allowed: Passive reconnaissance (public DNS, WHOIS, certificate transparency, search)
Active but non-destructive enumeration (port scan, service/version fingerprinting, subdomain brute-force at reasonable rate, directory/file enumeration)
Vulnerability probing (nuclei, nikto, safe wpscan, safe SQLi/XSS/SSRF/IDOR/auth probes)
Manual verification with a minimum proof-of-concept payload
forbidden: Credential stuffing / password spraying / brute force against production auth
Lateral movement / post-exploitation beyond minimum PoC
Data exfiltration beyond what is minimally required to prove impact (redact any real PII)
Testing against systems that appear to belong to third parties

rate_limits.principle: Low-and-slow. Prefer targeted queries over exhaustive brute force. Stop on 429/503 or clear WAF blocking; report and adapt.
